# `utils/FrustumCulling.js`

> **Source:** `editor/js/utils/FrustumCulling.js`

FrustumCulling.js — View-frustum culling for the editor viewport Overhauled to use AABB-vs-frustum (projection-interval / P-vertex method) which is far more accurate than bounding-sphere tests for non-uniform geometry (characters, vehicles, elongated props). Best practices applied (sources: LearnOpenGL Frustum Culling, Bruno Opsenica, GDBooks "3D Collisions", Frostbite GDC presentation): 1. Planes extracted from ViewProj matrix (Gribb-Hartmann), normalized once. 2. AABB test uses P-vertex method — only 1 dot product per plane. 3. Sphere test kept as fast broad-phase / fallback. 4. All data stored in flat Float32Array (cache-friendly, zero-alloc hot path). 5. Per-frame stats for profiling.

## Functions

### `extractFrustumPlanes(vp)`

Extract and normalize frustum planes from a 4×4 view-projection matrix. Uses Gribb-Hartmann method (column-major matrix). Must be called once per frame before any culling tests.

**Parameters:**

- `vp` *(Float32Array|number[])* — — column-major 4×4 ViewProj matrix

**Returns:** The 24-float plane array (reference — do NOT mutate)

### `isSphereInFrustum(center, radius, planes)`

Test if a bounding sphere is inside or intersects the frustum.

**Parameters:**

- `center` *(number[])* — [x, y, z] world-space sphere center
- `radius` *(number)* — sphere radius
- `[planes]` *(Float32Array)* — optional explicit planes (defaults to cached)

**Returns:** true if potentially visible

### `isAABBInFrustum(minX, minY, minZ, maxX, maxY, maxZ, planes)`

Test if a world-space AABB intersects the frustum. Uses the P-vertex method: for each plane pick the AABB corner most in the direction of the plane normal (the "positive" vertex). If that corner is behind the plane, the entire box is outside.

**Parameters:**

- `minX` *(number)* — @param {number} minY @param {number} minZ
- `maxX` *(number)* — @param {number} maxY @param {number} maxZ
- `[planes]` *(Float32Array)* — optional explicit planes

**Returns:** true if potentially visible

### `isAABBCenterExtentsInFrustum(cx, cy, cz, ex, ey, ez, planes)`

Convenience: test AABB from center + half-extents (world space). Converts to min/max and delegates.

### `isEntityAABBVisible(entityPos, entityScale, localCenter, localExtents, planes)`

High-level entity visibility test using AABB. Takes the mesh's local-space AABB center+extents, the entity's world position and scale, and produces the world-space AABB for frustum testing.

**Parameters:**

- `entityPos` *(number[])* — [x,y,z] entity world position
- `entityScale` *(number[])* — [sx,sy,sz]
- `localCenter` *(number[])* — mesh AABB center in local space
- `localExtents` *(number[])* — mesh AABB half-extents in local space
- `[planes]` *(Float32Array)* — _No description in source JSDoc._

### `isEntitySphereVisible(position, scale, baseRadius)`

Legacy: entity visibility using bounding sphere (kept for broad-phase / fallback).

### `getCullingStats()`

### `resetStats()`

### `getFrustumPlanes()`

Get current frustum planes (for debugging / external use)

### `getFrustumCorners(invViewProjMatrix)`

Calculate frustum corners in world space (for debug visualization)

**Parameters:**

- `invViewProjMatrix` *(Float32Array)* — Inverse view-projection matrix

**Returns:** 8 corner points

## Notes & Examples

### Editor Extension System

The editor supports extensions via the same Plauna component system as apps. Extensions can add panels, tools, menu items, and hooks into the engine. They run with elevated 'editor' capability granting access to the scene graph, asset database, and build pipeline.

**Example: Editor extension adding a custom panel**
```js
import { Extension } from 'editor/core/Extension.js';
import { Panel } from 'editor/ui/Panel.js';

class TerrainEditor extends Extension {
  id = 'terrain-editor';
  capabilities = ['editor', 'scene'];
  
  activate(context) {
    // Add menu item
    context.menus.add('Tools/Terrain', () => this.open());
    
    // Register tool
    context.tools.register('terrain', {
      icon: 'mountain',
      onSelect: (entity) => this.edit(entity)
    });
  }
  
  open() {
    this.panel = new Panel({
      title: 'Terrain Editor',
      content: this.buildUI()
    });
    context.workspace.addPanel(this.panel);
  }
  
  edit(entity) {
    const terrain = entity.get(TerrainComponent);
    this.panel.bind(terrain);
  }
}

editor.extensions.register(TerrainEditor);
```

**See also:** [Editor Overview](/editor/overview.md)
